title: Reversal of Roux-en-Y gastric bypass: A single center analysis
summary:
The Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB) is one of the most frequently performed bariatric procedures worldwide and has been successfully used for the treatment of obesity for decades. In recent years, however, the surgical reversal of this procedure has increasingly become a focus of clinical research. Although the overall rate is low, current literature indicates that in certain cases a restoration to the original gastrointestinal anatomy is medically indicated. In view of these research gaps, there is an urgent need for systematic investigation of indications, surgical techniques, short- and long-term outcomes, and other relevant parameters.

The aim of the planned study is therefore to assess the safety, efficacy, and patient satisfaction following RYGB reversal under real-world clinical conditions, thereby contributing to the optimization of indication criteria and follow-up care for this rare but clinically relevant procedure. With this study, we seek to investigate the extent to which reversal of the Roux-en-Y gastric bypass to the original anatomy affects parameters such as body weight, quality of life, and other complications.

interventions.name: All patients who underwent RYGB reversal at the Obesity Center Bad Krozingen since 2020

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All patients who have undergone RYGB reversal at our center since 2020
Exclusion criteria:
Age <18, lack of ability to consent
